meta.name: Define Link request and response schemas

context.data-model: Link(id integer pk, url text not null, title text null, created_at timestamp not null)
context.prd-excerpt:
Feature: Save a link (slug save-link).
User story: As someone collecting links, I want to store a URL with an optional title, so that I can come back to it without keeping a browser tab open.
Description: A POST endpoint that accepts a URL and an optional title, stores it, and returns the stored record including its generated id and creation timestamp.
The URL is the only required field. If no title is supplied the field is stored as null rather than being derived from the page, because fetching the page would make the endpoint depend on the network.
Considerations (from the feature's notes, not an acceptance criterion): duplicate URLs are allowed. Deduplication needs a rule for what to do with the existing record's tags and timestamp, and that decision is out of scope.

task.objective: Define the two Pydantic v2 models that carry link payloads over HTTP: LinkCreate for the request body of POST /links, and LinkRead for the response body of POST /links and GET /links. LinkCreate's url validation is the mechanism L3-003 later relies on to produce 422 for save-link criteria 3 and 4, and it must reject before any database session is touched - which it does by construction, because FastAPI validates the request body before the handler function is entered. This task builds the mechanism only; it asserts neither criterion, and L3-003 is where both are tested end to end.

requirements.requirement: Define class `LinkCreate(BaseModel)` with exactly two fields: - url: str (required - no default, so a missing url is a validation error) - title: str | None (optional - defaults to None)

On `LinkCreate`, define a Pydantic v2 field validator for `url` that rejects any value which is not an absolute http or https URL. Implement it with `urllib.parse.urlparse`, and raise `ValueError("url must be an absolute http or https URL")` when either of these holds: - the parsed scheme is not exactly "http" or "https" (so "ftp://example.com/x" and "javascript:alert(1)" are rejected), or - the parsed netloc is empty (so "/relative/path", "not-a-url" and "http://" are rejected). Use the decorator form: @field_validator("url") @classmethod def _url_must_be_absolute_http(cls, value: str) -> str: ... Return the value unchanged when it passes. Do not strip, lowercase, or otherwise rewrite the url - callers get back exactly what they submitted.
Type the field as `str`. Do NOT type it as pydantic's `HttpUrl` or `AnyHttpUrl`. Pydantic v2 normalises those types and appends a trailing slash to a bare-authority URL ("https://example.com" becomes "https://example.com/"), which would make the endpoint return a url that is not the one submitted and break save-link criterion 1 ("the submitted url") in L3-003.
Define class `LinkRead(BaseModel)` with exactly four fields: - id: int - url: str - title: str | None - created_at: datetime (from the stdlib `datetime` module)

Give `LinkRead` the model config `model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)` so that FastAPI can serialise a SQLAlchemy `Link` ORM instance returned directly from a route handler. L3-003 returns the ORM object, not a dict, and without this config that raises a validation error at response time.

`title` on `LinkRead` must be a nullable field that is always PRESENT in the serialised output. Do not mark it with `exclude=True` and do not configure `response_model_exclude_none`. save-link criterion 2 and list-links criterion 3 both require an untitled link to report `"title": null` rather than omit the key.

test-requirements.test:
Test-first. Write every test below into `tests/test_link_schemas.py` BEFORE writing `app/schemas/link.py`, run `pytest tests/test_link_schemas.py` and watch them fail on the missing import, then write the schemas until they pass. Runner: pytest.
Imports for the file: `pytest`, `from datetime import datetime`, `import types`, `from pydantic import ValidationError` and `from app.schemas.link import LinkCreate, LinkRead`.

Test: test_link_create_rejects_missing_url - Call `LinkCreate.model_validate({})` inside `pytest.raises(ValidationError)` - Call `LinkCreate.model_validate({"title": "A title but no url"})` inside `pytest.raises(ValidationError)` - On the second call, capture the exception as `exc_info` and assert that `"url"` appears in `[error["loc"][0] for error in exc_info.value.errors()]`, so the failure is attributed to the url field and not to some other field - This test cites no acceptance criterion; it asserts requirement 2's "required, no default". save-link#3 says the system shall return 422 and store nothing, and this test observes neither a status code nor a row count - it observes a ValidationError from a model in isolation. L3-003 owns the end-to-end test for that criterion.

Test: test_link_create_rejects_non_absolute_http_url - For each of these values, assert `LinkCreate.model_validate({"url": value})` raises `ValidationError`: "not-a-url" "/relative/path" "example.com" "ftp://example.com/file.txt" "javascript:alert(1)" "http://" "" - Then, in the same test, assert the validator is not rejecting everything: for each of these values, `LinkCreate.model_validate({"url": value})` must succeed and the resulting model's `.url` must equal the value unchanged: "http://example.com" "https://example.com" "https://example.com/a/b?c=d#e" "https://sub.example.co.uk:8443/path" - The unchanged-value assertion is what proves no normalisation is happening; a trailing slash appearing on "https://example.com" means requirement 3 was implemented with pydantic's HttpUrl type instead of a str plus validator - This test cites no acceptance criterion; it asserts requirement 3's validator directly. As with test 2, save-link#4 is a statement about a 422 response and an unchanged row count, and this test observes neither. L3-003 owns the end-to-end test for it.

Test: test_link_create_accepts_absent_title_as_none - Assert `LinkCreate.model_validate({"url": "https://example.com"}).title is None` - Assert `LinkCreate.model_validate({"url": "https://example.com", "title": None}).title is None` - Assert `LinkCreate.model_validate({"url": "https://example.com", "title": "Hello"}).title == "Hello"` - This test cites no acceptance criterion. It guards the optionality that save-link criterion 2 depends on, but criterion 2 is a statement about the endpoint returning 201, which this task does not build; L3-003 owns the test for it. Recorded here rather than attributed to a criterion it does not actually assert.

Test: test_link_read_serialises_null_title_as_a_present_key - Build `LinkRead(id=1, url="https://example.com", title=None, created_at=datetime(2026, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5))` - Assert `"title" in model.model_dump()` - Assert `model.model_dump()["title"] is None` - Assert `model.model_dump()["id"] == 1` and that it is an `int` - This test cites no acceptance criterion; it asserts requirement 6 directly. The criteria about null titles in a response (save-link#2, list-links#3) are asserted end-to-end in L3-003 and L3-004.

Test: test_link_read_reads_from_object_attributes - Define a plain local class inside the test with attributes id, url, title, created_at (a `types.SimpleNamespace` is sufficient and needs no new import beyond `types`) - Assert `LinkRead.model_validate(that_object).url == "https://example.com"` - This proves requirement 5's `from_attributes=True` is set; without it this call raises ValidationError. Cites no criterion - it asserts the ORM-compatibility contract that L3-003 relies on.

verification.step: Run: `python -c "from app.schemas.link import LinkCreate, LinkRead"` - must exit 0 with no output
Run: `pytest tests/test_link_schemas.py -v` - all 5 test functions pass
Run: `python -c "from app.schemas.link import LinkCreate; print(LinkCreate.model_validate({'url': 'https://example.com'}).url)"` - must print exactly `https://example.com` with no trailing slash
Verify: `app/schemas/link.py` contains no import of `HttpUrl` or `AnyHttpUrl` from pydantic

exports.interface:
from pydantic import BaseModel, field_validator
class LinkCreate(BaseModel): """Request body for POST /links.""" url: str # required; must be an absolute http or https URL title: str | None # optional; defaults to None
# Rejects any url whose scheme is not http/https or whose netloc is empty. # Raises pydantic.ValidationError at request-parse time, before any route # handler runs, so nothing is ever written to the database for a bad payload.

from datetime import datetime from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict
class LinkRead(BaseModel): """Response body for POST /links and each element of GET /links.""" model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)
id: int url: str title: str | None # always present in the serialised output, null when unset created_at: datetime
# from_attributes=True means a route handler may return the SQLAlchemy Link ORM # instance directly and FastAPI will serialise it against this model.
